title: verify and doctor

story: Nova, our ticket-to-PR agent, is working on RH-1234, the "No projects yet" card for an empty projects table. The ticket asks for the workgroup's name on the card, so Nova adds a workgroup argument to the small function that builds the card's text, updates that function's test, runs the test file, sees it pass, and writes "Done, tests pass".

Twelve minutes later the pull request's type check is red. A second file, the projects page, still calls the function with one argument. Nova did not lie: the test it ran did pass. It simply ran a different set of checks than CI runs, and nothing made it run the others before it said done. A person would have made the same mistake, because today a frontend change needs four separate commands, and everyone picks a few.
hook.question: How do we give people, Nova and CI one command that gives the answer CI will give, and make sure the agent runs it before it says done?

read.h: One command that answers like CI
p: Today fcp's frontend has separate scripts for lint, the type check and the unit tests, and CI runs all of them on every file. Locally that is slow, so people run a part of it, and an agent does the same. The plan adds one script, npm run verify, that answers the question CI will ask, but only about what changed. It looks at the files that changed since the merge base (the commit where the branch left main), plus new files git does not track yet, and runs three steps.

The steps are not all narrowed the same way, and that is the important design choice. Biome, the linter and formatter fcp uses, only needs the changed files, because a lint error lives inside one file. Vitest has a command, vitest related, that takes a list of source files and runs every test that imports them, directly or through other files, so a change to the card's text also runs the projects page's tests. But the type check always runs on the whole project, because types cross file boundaries: the error in the story is in a file Nova never touched. At the end the script prints one line per step and exits with 1 if any step failed, which keeps the answer small enough for an agent to read.

code.file: scripts/verify.ts (the lab version; fcp's is frontend/scripts/verify.ts)

notes.text: The merge base with main. VERIFY_BASE lets you compare with something else, for example a release branch.
Added, copied, modified or renamed files, so a deleted file is not handed to Biome.
New files that git does not track yet count as changed too.
The type check is never narrowed: it always checks the whole project.
--all is for CI: lint everything and run the whole unit suite.
Only the tests that import a changed file. No related test is not a failure.
The exit code is the answer. Everything that calls verify only reads this.

verify: 2 changed files since 0e67403
pass  lint
FAIL  types
pass  related unit tests

read.h: Not done while verify is red
p: A command only helps if it runs. Writing "always run npm run verify" into the agent's instructions is a rule the model may forget after an hour of work. A hook cannot be forgotten. Claude Code runs a hook, a command you configure, at fixed moments of a session, and the Stop hook runs every time the agent wants to end its turn. If the hook exits with code 2, Claude Code does not end the turn: it gives the agent whatever the hook wrote to stderr as its next message, so the agent reads "FAIL types" and goes back to work. Exit 0 lets it stop. Any other code counts as a broken hook, and the agent stops anyway.

One field in the hook's input prevents an endless loop. stop_hook_active is true when the agent is already trying again because this hook blocked it once. Then the hook reports and lets the session end, so a problem the agent cannot fix goes to a person instead of spending tokens forever.

The hook is registered in fcp's .claude/settings.json, the project settings file that is committed to the repo. That is the reason one hook is enough. Every engineer who opens fcp in Claude Code gets it, and so does Nova, because Nova's harness, our program that runs the Claude session in the VM, loads fcp's project settings. Nova's own hooks then only check what is special to Nova, such as proof for each check in its approved plan.

code.text:
#!/bin/bash
# fcp's Stop hook, for people and for Nova: run the verify of every area that changed.
input=$(cat)
if [ "$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.stop_hook_active')" = "true" ]; then
  echo "verify is still red after one more try; ending so a person can look" >&2
  exit 0
fi
cd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"
changed=$( { git diff --name-only "$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)"; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard; } )
report=""
if grep -q '^frontend/' <<<"$changed"; then
  report+="$(cd frontend && npm run verify --silent 2>&1)"$'\n' || failed=1
fi
if grep -qE '^(cloud|client|common|sdk)/' <<<"$changed"; then
  report+="$(uvx --from poethepoet poe verify 2>&1)"$'\n' || failed=1
fi
[ -z "$failed" ] && exit 0
grep -E '^(pass|FAIL) ' <<<"$report" >&2
echo "verify failed. Backend details: cloud/rhinoCloud/reports/failures.md" >&2
exit 2

notes.text: The second stop in a row: report and let it end instead of looping.
The same changed files verify uses: since the merge base, plus untracked files.
Each area runs its own verify: npm run verify for the frontend.
And poe verify for the backend areas. poe is the Python version of npm scripts.
Only the summary lines go to stderr, so the agent gets a few lines, not a 3,000-line log.
Code 2: the agent does not stop, and it gets the lines above as its next message.

p: The last caller is CI. If CI keeps its own separate lint, type and test steps, the two lists will slowly drift apart: someone adds a check to CI and forgets verify, and green on a laptop stops meaning green on the PR. So the frontend's unit-tests job runs npm run verify -- --all in place of its three separate steps, and the backend's API test job runs poe verify --all. --all means the same steps on every file, which is what CI should check anyway.

So the contract between fcp, Nova and CI is small: one command per area, a few summary lines, and an exit code. Nobody shares code with anybody. If the frontend team changes what verify runs, the editor, Nova and CI all change on the same day, because they all call the same name.

deeper.h: Go deeper: poe verify picks its own test set
p: The backend version follows the same shape in Python. It lints the changed .py files with pre-commit, which runs black, isort and flake8, and runs the API tests that the change touched, through pytest-testmon from the API test layer lesson. A few paths force the whole API layer instead: migrations, fixtures and the layer's conftest.py. testmon cannot see them, because they are read while the test database is built, before any test runs, so a change there would otherwise run no tests at all.
Changes in sdk/ run the SDK's own make lint test. The on-prem client has no fast test layer yet, so for now its step is still open: lint only, or the slower unit tests in Docker.

read.h: doctor: can this machine run verify at all?
p: Green only means the same everywhere if every machine can run the same command. A missing Python version, an old Node, a virtual environment that no longer matches the lockfile: each of these makes verify fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the change, and a new joiner or a fresh virtual machine (VM) for an agent run meets all of them on the first day. poe doctor is the second command. It checks the machine against what fcp asks for (Node and npm from frontend/package.json, Python 3.13 through uv, the backend's virtual environment against uv.lock, enough Docker memory for FCP Lab, the full product on one machine) and prints ok, or FIX with the command to try. With --fix it runs only the safe fixes, such as installing a Python version, and it never touches credentials, ~/.aws or Docker volumes.

The doctor also reports one problem that surprises people. When npm install runs in frontend/, husky, the tool that installs the frontend's git hooks, sets git's core.hooksPath to its own folder, so the backend's black, isort and flake8 commit hooks never run for anyone. The doctor says so and points to poe verify.
read.see:
ok   node >=24.15.0
ok   Python 3.13 (uv)
FIX  cloud venv = uv.lock  -> make -C cloud/rhinoCloud sync-deps
ok   Docker >= 16 GiB (FCP Lab)
FIX  Python commit hooks (husky owns core.hooksPath, so black/isort/flake8 never run)  -> run `poe verify` before you push
(example output; your machine differs)

deeper.h: Go deeper: the doctor runs every night
p: The machine image that every agent's VM starts from is built every night on a brand-new machine, which makes the build the best test of a fresh setup there is. After the fcp checkout and the dependency install, the build runs poe doctor --json as the user Nova runs as, keeps the report next to the image, and fails if any check failed. A failed build is not promoted, so the VMs keep yesterday's image, and the alert names the failing checks. When the doctor fails there, people's laptops usually meet the same problem a few days later, so it is an early warning for the whole team.

lab.title: One verify, and a Stop hook that waits for it
needs: No Claude session: you feed the hook the same JSON Claude Code would send
lab.goal: Build npm run verify for a small TypeScript project, watch it catch a type error that the agent's own test run missed, and make a Stop hook turn that red into "keep working".

guess.q: The agent changes emptyStateText(count) to emptyStateText(count, workgroup) and updates its own test. The projects page still calls it with one argument. Which check fails?

options.text: vitest run src/emptyState.test.ts, the test the agent ran.
options.why: That test was updated together with the function, so it passes.

options.text: vitest related, because it also runs the projects page's test.
options.why: It does run that test, but Vitest does not type-check. At run time the missing argument is just undefined, and the page's test only checks a non-empty list.

options.text: tsc, the type check, which reads every file in the project.
options.why: Only the type checker sees that a file nobody touched now calls the function with too few arguments.

follow.say: Write the Stop hook and feed it the JSON Claude Code sends when the agent wants to stop. Exit 2 means "not yet", and the lines on stderr become the agent's next message.
follow.do:
cat > scripts/stop-verify.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Claude Code Stop hook: Claude may stop only when verify is green. Exit 2 sends it back to work.
input=$(cat)
if [ "$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.stop_hook_active')" = "true" ]; then
  echo "verify was already asked for once; letting the session end" >&2
  exit 0
fi
if ! out=$(npm run verify --silent 2>&1); then
  echo "$out" | grep -E '^(pass|FAIL) ' >&2
  echo "npm run verify failed. Fix the steps marked FAIL, then stop again." >&2
  exit 2
fi
exit 0
EOF
chmod +x scripts/stop-verify.sh
echo '{"hook_event_name": "Stop", "stop_hook_active": false}' | scripts/stop-verify.sh; echo "exit=$?"
follow.see:
pass  lint
FAIL  types
pass  related unit tests
npm run verify failed. Fix the steps marked FAIL, then stop again.
exit=2

follow.say: Register the hook in the project settings that are committed with the code, so every person and agent that opens this folder in Claude Code gets it.
Do what the agent does after the hook sends it back: fix the page that still calls the function with one argument, then try to stop again.

lab.build: verify narrows the tests to the files that import a change, but some files change every test without being imported by any: package.json, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json and vitest.config.ts. Prove the hole first. Create vitest.config.ts with import { defineConfig } from "vitest/config"; export default defineConfig({ test: { include: ["src/**/*.spec.ts"] } }), which quietly matches no test file at all, and run npm run verify: everything passes. Then add a FULL_RUN list of those four files to verify.ts, and when any of them changed, run the whole suite (vitest run) instead of the related tests. Run verify again: the unit tests step now fails with "No test files found". Delete vitest.config.ts and verify is green again.
checks: npm run verify on the clean branch prints "0 changed files" and runs only the type check.
After the agent's change, verify prints FAIL types and exits with 1, while vitest run src/emptyState.test.ts alone passes.
The hook exits with 2 and prints the summary lines while verify is red, and exits with 0 when stop_hook_active is true.
After you fix projectsPage.ts the hook exits with 0.
With your FULL_RUN rule, a change to vitest.config.ts makes verify run the whole suite and show FAIL unit tests.
lab.fix: A teammate tidied the hook: it now prints verify's summary with a plain echo and ends with exit 1 "because 1 means failure". Make that change in scripts/stop-verify.sh, break projectsPage.ts again, and feed the hook the stop_hook_active false input. It exits with 1 and the summary goes to stdout. In Claude Code, exit 1 is a non-blocking error and stdout is not shown to the agent, so the agent stops with a red type check and never sees why. Put the summary back on stderr (>&2) and the exit code back to 2.
explain: Why does verify narrow lint and tests to the changed files but always run the type check on the whole project?
What do exit 0, exit 2 and exit 1 from a Stop hook each do to the agent, and why does the hook look at stop_hook_active?
Why does CI run npm run verify -- --all instead of keeping its own lint, type and test steps?
lab.done: verify catches the type error the agent's own test missed, the hook turns it into exit 2 and lets go on the second try, and your FULL_RUN rule catches a config change that no related test would see.

check.q: A teammate suggests making verify faster by type-checking only the changed files, like lint. What goes wrong?

options.text: Nothing, because a type error is always in the file that changed.
options.why: The story's error is in the projects page, a file nobody changed. It broke because a function it calls changed.

options.text: A changed function can break the files that call it, and those files would not be checked.
options.why: Types cross file boundaries, so the type check has to read the whole project to see every caller.

options.text: tsc refuses to run on a list of files.
options.why: tsc can be given files. The problem is what such a run would miss, not whether it runs.

check.q: Nova's harness, the program that runs its Claude session in the VM, loads fcp's project settings. Why does that matter for the Stop hook?

options.text: It lets Nova change the hook when it is in the way.
options.why: The settings file is a protected path. Loading it means Nova obeys it, not that Nova may edit it.

options.text: It makes the hook run faster in the VM.
options.why: Speed is the same. The point is which hook runs.

options.text: Nova runs the very same verify hook as every engineer, so there is one hook to maintain and one meaning of green.
options.why: fcp's committed .claude/settings.json is the one place the hook lives. People, Nova and CI then all call the same command.

check.q: The agent stops twice in a row while verify is still red. On the second stop, stop_hook_active is true. What should the hook do?

options.text: Report the problem and exit 0, so the session ends and a person can look.
options.why: One more try is useful; an endless loop is not. The red result is still visible in the run's evidence.

options.text: Exit 2 again, until verify is green.
options.why: If the agent cannot fix it, this loops forever and keeps spending tokens.

options.text: Run verify with --all to be sure.
options.why: A bigger check does not help the agent fix the first one. The question is whether to keep blocking.

p: frontend/scripts/verify.ts with "verify": "node scripts/verify.ts" (Node 24 runs .ts directly, and CI rejects new .js or .mjs files): biome check on the changed files, tsc --noEmit on the project, vitest related --run --passWithNoTests on changed src/ and test/ files, and --all with VITEST_MONOCART=1 for coverage in CI. Whether stories of changed components also run (option A: @storybook/addon-vitest, option B: a render smoke test per changed *.stories.tsx) is for the FE guild, and frontend/AGENTS.md gets a short rule: tests assert on what the user sees (test ids, ARIA roles and names, visible text, row counts), never class names.

scripts/poe_verify.py is a poe script task in the root pyproject.toml (pre-commit on changed .py files, poe api-test when migrations, fixtures or tests_api/conftest.py changed, otherwise poe api-test-affected, make -C sdk lint test for sdk/; decide with the BE guild whether client/ gets lint only or the Docker-based unit tests). scripts/claude_stop_verify.sh and the Stop entry live in fcp's tracked .claude/settings.json; Nova's harness (the program that runs its Claude session in the VM) loads it through settingSources ["project"], so Nova's own Stop hook only checks proof for the plan's QA checks. CI: API Tests runs uvx --from poethepoet poe verify --all, and frontend-ci's unit-tests job runs npm run verify -- --all in place of lint, check-types and test:unit:coverage. scripts/poe_doctor.py reads frontend/package.json engines (node >=24.15.0, npm >=11.14.1), checks uv sync --check, Docker memory of 16 GiB and the rhino-net network, and reports husky's core.hooksPath; the nightly build of ai-agent-sandbox, the VM image, runs poe doctor --json as the sandbox user, keeps doctor.jsonl and fails the build so the image is not promoted.

tickets.why: npm run verify for the frontend: changed files, the three steps and the one-line summary.
poe verify, the shared Stop hook in fcp's project settings, and CI calling the same commands.
poe doctor: the setup checks, safe --fix, --json and the husky hooks finding.
poe doctor --json in the nightly sandbox image build; a failure keeps yesterday's image.

words.plain: One command per area that checks what changed since main the way CI would, and answers with an exit code.
The commit where your branch left main; verify compares the branch with it.
A Vitest command that runs every test importing the given files, directly or through other files.
A command Claude Code runs when the agent wants to end its turn; exit 2 sends the agent back to work.
True in the hook's input when the agent is already trying again because a Stop hook blocked it.
A command that checks whether a machine can run the project at all, and suggests or applies safe fixes.

review.q: Explain to a teammate in three sentences why one verify command beats four separate scripts plus a line in the agent's instructions.
review.a: The editor, the agent and CI call the same command, so green means the same everywhere and the lists cannot drift apart. The Stop hook runs it whenever the agent wants to stop, which a written instruction cannot promise. Its short summary and exit code are all any caller needs.

review.q: Which files make the backend's poe verify run the whole API layer instead of the affected tests, and why?
review.a: Migrations, fixtures and tests_api/conftest.py: they are read while the test database is built, before any test runs, so testmon cannot connect them to tests.

review.q: The nightly sandbox image build fails on poe doctor. What happens to the agent VMs the next morning?
review.a: The new image is not promoted, so VMs keep starting from yesterday's image, and the alert names the failing checks so the owner can fix the setup.

remember: One verify per area, called the same way by the editor, Nova's Stop hook and CI, and a doctor that proves each machine can run it.
